description: Envoy proxy monitoring Dashboard with cluster and service level templates. Adapted from Envoy Gateway (Apache-2.0, https://github.com/envoyproxy/gateway); modified. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md.

panels.title: Live servers
panels.description: Envoy proxies reporting live now. Zero means no data plane is serving; compare with the number of proxy pods you expect.

panels.title: Avg uptime per node
panels.description: Average time the proxies have been running. A value that keeps resetting is a crash loop or repeated restarts: read the proxy pods' events.

panels.title: Allocated Memory
panels.description: Envoy heap memory in use, per proxy. Compare with the pod's memory limit; a steady climb is a leak or a growing configuration.

panels.title: Heap Size
panels.description: Envoy heap memory reserved from the operating system, per proxy. Compare with the pod's memory limit.

panels.title: Unhealthy Clusters
panels.description: Endpoints that are known to the selected Envoy cluster and not healthy. Should be zero; if not, the panels below name the cluster.

panels.title: Cluster State
panels.description: One when every endpoint of the selected clusters is healthy, zero otherwise.

panels.title: Total active connections
panels.description: Connections open from the proxies to each selected Envoy cluster. A steady climb is connections not being closed.

panels.title: Total requests
panels.description: Requests per second sent to each selected Envoy cluster. A cluster at zero that should carry traffic is unrouted.

panels.title: Upstream Network Traffic
panels.description: Bytes per second received from and sent to each selected Envoy cluster (received above, sent below, per series). A cluster with requests and no bytes returns empty answers.

panels.title: Downstream Network Traffic
panels.description: Bytes per second received from and sent to clients on HTTP listeners. The client side of the traffic in the panel beside it.

panels.title: Upstream Latency
panels.description: Request latency at p50, p90 and p99 for each selected Envoy cluster, in milliseconds. One cluster far above the others is a slow backend.

panels.title: Upstream 2xx Responses
panels.description: Responses per second with a 2xx status from each selected Envoy cluster. The healthy baseline.

panels.title: Upstream 4xx Responses
panels.description: Responses per second with a 4xx status from each selected Envoy cluster. A rise is a broken route, auth policy or a client sending bad requests.

panels.title: Downstream members
panels.description: Healthy endpoints in the selected Envoy clusters, in total and per cluster; the second panel adds the unhealthy count. A fall is backends leaving or failing health checks.

panels.title: Upstream 5xx Responses
panels.description: Responses per second with a 5xx status from each selected Envoy cluster. Should be near zero; the cluster with the rate is the failing backend.

panels.title: Upstream 3xx Responses
panels.description: Responses per second with a 3xx status from each selected Envoy cluster (redirects).

panels.title: Downstream members
panels.description: Healthy endpoints in the selected Envoy clusters, in total and per cluster; the second panel adds the unhealthy count. A fall is backends leaving or failing health checks.

panels.title: Degraded
panels.description: Endpoints marked degraded, per Envoy cluster: still receiving traffic at a reduced share.

panels.title: Excluded
panels.description: Endpoints excluded from load balancing, per Envoy cluster, for example while draining.
